CANONICAL_NAME.value: MiniSat 1.14 (2006) -- the small CDCL solver in its pre-2.0 form (Een & Sorensson)

value.lineage: SAT lineage, the PREDECESSOR of the vault's minisat-2.2.0: 1.14 is the version described in 'An Extensible SAT-solver' (SAT 2003) as it stood in 2006 -- ~600 lines of core, before 2.0's rewrite (SimpSolver, new restart/reduce policies). Beside zchaff-2007 (the rival it displaced) and 2.2.0 (its successor) the vault holds the transition.

value.built_to: be the smallest complete CDCL solver competitive with the large ones, so others could extend it
value.pressure: the SAT competitions; the size and opacity of Chaff-era solvers
value.success_means: correct SAT/UNSAT; extensibility that made it the base of a generation of solvers

value.failure_condition: a wrong answer; a heuristic regression versus rivals

ANCESTRY.value: SAT lineage, the PREDECESSOR of the vault's minisat-2.2.0: 1.14 is the version described in 'An Extensible SAT-solver' (SAT 2003) as it stood in 2006 -- ~600 lines of core, before 2.0's rewrite (SimpSolver, new restart/reduce policies). Beside zchaff-2007 (the rival it displaced) and 2.2.0 (its successor) the vault holds the transition.

evidence.ref: Een & Sorensson, An Extensible SAT-solver, SAT 2003
evidence.says: Describes the MiniSat core that 1.14 represents.
The 2.x line rewrote the solver (SimpSolver, new restart and clause-reduction policies) and replaced the 1.x line.

ancestry_edges.note: direction: MiniSat superseded zChaff (recorded on both records)
